signal_or_failure: membership fee revenue up 12 percent on signups at new units and a strong base
what_it_demonstrated: that customers were being recruited in volume alongside units and that the fee was being accepted
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: that members renewed - no renewal rate exists anywhere in this corpus
notes: The only in-window causal statement about customers.

signal_or_failure: a third party's ability to name the format at all: membership wholesale or big box retail
what_it_demonstrated: that by 1991 the format was recognisable enough that a planning office used two genre labels for it without defining them
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: that any individual customer valued it - the labels come from a traffic analysis
notes: The only in-window independent evidence that the product existed as a category, and it is the kind of signal no company filing can supply.

signal_or_failure: roughly ten million memberships across two classes
what_it_demonstrated: that the member base behind the fee line is large and mostly individual rather than business (6.7M Gold Star to 3.3M Business)
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: (PB) and demonstrates nothing about Stage 1; it also reverses the assumption that a business-membership format is dominated by businesses
notes: Recorded because the class split contradicts an inherited shorthand and a later pass should see that early.

signal_or_failure: a member base large enough for a city to estimate in-window: 31000 San Francisco Costco members already shopping outside the city
what_it_demonstrated: that leg C had enough members in one undeveloped market for a planning office to treat car-borne demand as material
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: that the members were profitable or renewed, that the store was built, or that San Francisco was typical
notes: The only membership evidence inside Stage 1 in this corpus and the only validation signal no company wrote.
